Patients diagnosed with any form of diabetic macular edema or advanced diabetic retinopathy should be referred to an ophthalmologist without delay for specialized evaluation and management. 10. Panretinal laser photocoagulation is an effective intervention to reduce the risk of vision loss in individuals with high-risk proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR). 11. Intravitreal injections of anti-VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor) agents are recommended for the treatment of diabetic macular edema to enhance visual acuity and slow the progression of the disease. 12. Anti-VEGF therapy is considered the first-line treatment for diabetic macular edema due to its efficacy in improving visual outcomes. 13. Focal or grid laser therapy, as well as corticosteroid injections, are viable therapeutic options for patients with significant diabetic macular edema, depending on the clinical scenario. 14. The use of aspirin for cardioprotection is not contraindicated in patients with retinopathy and does not increase the risk of retinal or systemic bleeding.
